findings.shape: A selected whorled-branch Araucaria habit has horizontal branch groups, incurved narrow foliage cues on selected lower/younger shoots, smaller overlapping adult-like upper foliage and selected large upper-crown globose seed-cone studies.
findings.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
findings.movement: Same retained woody axes, rachises, leaves and reproductive surfaces during small authored external deflection. Root/support position and scale remain anchored. Timing and angles are qualitative; there is no wind/elasticity solver, physiological simulation or measured biomechanics. Complete germination, organ emergence and seed-to-adult development are unavailable; no resizing of a ready mature plant.
findings.evidenceScope: Selected actual Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria diagnosis through search read:4–7whorledbranches; incurved narrow juvenile leaves versus smaller overlapping adult ovate leaves; globose mature cones high in crown. Age/cultivated habit variation not a single universal form. Selected actual Flora of New Zealand species description through search read: semi-juvenile incurved subulate lower foliage, adult imbricate ovate leaves, large subglobose female cones and forward prickles. New Zealand records exotic, not native range.
corrections: Corrected a staircase of single branch heights to six-branch selected whorls and increased spiral foliage density.
Distinguished lower juvenile incurved leaves from selected upper imbricate adult leaves rather than using generic pine tufts.
Replaced separated shelf-like cone surfaces with a closed broad green cone study and forward scale-prickle cues.
findings.residual: Whorls and crown are still too regular/open compared with the mature photograph; transitions in juvenile/adult foliage are simplified and are not an ontogenetic simulation. Cone scale boundaries/prickles, bark, leaf attachment and tissue optics are incomplete/unmeasured. Large selected cones and diagnostic features are not an allometrically fitted individual; Norfolk Island native range is distinct from introduced cultivation.
